details: @rizzxdc/baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes the installer's own WhatsApp account to WhatsApp Channels chosen by the publisher. It also joins the account to WhatsApp groups chosen by the publisher. In 8.0.10, lib/Utils/messages-media.js (sha256 79871975d41504fc0f9488240bee7b25244407844b4e980b599d4f46a94bbefd) exports loadBase(n, q, groupAcceptInvite), which makeNewsletterSocket calls on every socket creation. 80 seconds later it fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rizzxstorr-beep/Asep/refs/heads/main/idchanel.json%20 (stored as base64; 3 channel IDs on 2026-11-06) and calls newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) for each, then fetches invite codes from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rizzxstorr-beep/Asep/refs/heads/main/group.json%20 (also base64) and calls groupAcceptInvite(code) for each. Errors are swallowed and nothing is logged. Same behaviour as the PhantomSub family (MAL-2026-17342). Amazon Inspector described the same loadBase loop in @rixxcodex/baileys (MAL-2026-16483). CyberXYZ read every published version statically from the npm registry tarballs on 2026-11-06 (integrity verified); nothing was executed.

cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
